# Texas Law Review

> A premier academic law journal publishing rigorous legal scholarship on constitutional law, corporate governance, and contemporary legal issues.

Texas Law Review is a leading legal publication affiliated with the University of Texas that accepts article submissions, sells journal subscriptions and single issues, and hosts symposia on important legal topics. The journal maintains editorial standards through The Greenbook and Manual on Usage & Style, and uses Scholastica for submission management.

## Key Topics

- Constitutional Law
- Legal Analysis
- Article Submissions
- Journal Subscriptions
- Corporate Governance
- Tax Law
- Separation of Powers
- Supreme Court Ethics
- Nonprofit Accountability
- Federal Firearms Law
- Submission Guidelines
- Author Requirements
- Reference Guides

- Manual on Usage & Style

## Featured Legal Analysis

- [Applying History as Law: The Role of Historical Facts in Implementing Constitutional Doctrine](https://texaslawreview.org/applying-history-as-law-the-role-of-historical-facts-in-implementing-constitutional-doctrine): Blocher and Garrett on historical interpretation in constitutional doctrine
- [The Singular Role of Public Pension Funds in Corporate Governance](https://texaslawreview.org/the-singular-role-of-public-pension-funds-in-corporate-governance): Fisch and Schwartz examine public pension funds' corporate governance role
- [The State of Charity Care in the United States: Holding Nonprofit Hospitals Accountable for Their Tax Exemptions](https://texaslawreview.org/the-state-of-charity-care-in-the-united-states-holding-nonprofit-hospitals-accountable-for-their-tax-exemptions): Tran analyzes nonprofit hospital accountability for tax exemptions
- [Right Diagnosis, Wrong Cure: Reconceptualizing the Commerce Clause Basis for the Federal Prohibition on Felon Firearm Possession](https://texaslawreview.org/right-diagnosis-wrong-cure-reconceptualizing-the-commerce-clause-basis-for-the-federal-prohibition-on-felon-firearm-possession): Klein examines Commerce Clause basis for federal felon firearm prohibition
- [The Behavioral Case for Supreme Court Ethics Reform](https://texaslawreview.org/the-behavioral-case-for-supreme-court-ethics-reform): Panuska applies behavioral analysis to Supreme Court ethics reform
- [Delegation Running Ratchet](https://texaslawreview.org/delegation-running-ratchet): Diedrich explores nondelegation doctrine and separation of powers issues
- [Who Authorizes the Authorizers: The Problem with Professor Markovits's Jurisprudence](https://texaslawreview.org/who-authorizes-the-authorizers-the-problem-with-professor-markovitss-jurisprudence): Nyberg critiques Markovits's constitutional jurisprudence and authority
- [Catching Pokémon, Not Tax Bills](https://texaslawreview.org/catching-pokemon-not-tax-bills): Narotzki and Shanan analyze tax law implications of Pokémon Go
